terms.gloss: turn away, turn aside; ward off, avert; carry off
evidence: Caes. BC 3.59: praedam omnem domum āvertēbant (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: turned away, with the back turned; disinclined, unfriendly, hostile
evidence: Verg. A. 2.170: āversa deae mēns (Lewis & Short)
Hor. S. 1.5.29: āversōs solitī compōnere amīcōs (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: malī culicēs rānaeque palūstrēs āvertunt somnōs
phrases.english: the wicked mosquitoes and the marsh frogs drive sleep away
they were carrying all the plunder off home

phrases.latin: āversōs bovēs eximium quemque pulchritūdine caudīs in spēluncam trāxit
phrases.english: he dragged the finest of the cattle backwards by their tails into the cave
used to reconciling friends who have fallen out

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections, checked against the editions named there.
